lines.li: {X_nameDef} played for the whole colony after supper, one tune running into the next, and the last of them went to bed humming.
[winter] With the shutters closed and the stove going, {X_nameDef} played for the whole colony until the candles were stubs. {A_nameDef} asked for the slow one twice.
{X_nameDef} played a few tunes at supper for {X_possessive} bed, the way traveling players do, and was gone again in the morning.

On {X_nameDef}'s advice, {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} were set to the woodpile side by side. By the end of the afternoon the logs were split, and so was the work between them, without anyone telling them how.
{X_nameDef} is thanked and told the colony settles its own quarrels. {X_nameDef} glances over at {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef}, and says nothing more about it.
The envoys from {FACTION} were given the colony's best and every answer they asked for, down to who mends the roof and who decided they should. They went home to {PLACE} with full notebooks.
The envoys are told the council meets behind a shut door. They take it well, sleep the night as guests, and go home to {PLACE} with nothing to write down.
{X_nameDef} takes the bowl with both hands, eats with the drum across {X_possessive} knees, and goes on to sing for some other camp.
{X_nameDef} took pictures of the colony at its work all day, and paid half of {COUNT} silver for the right to print them. {A_nameDef} has asked to be sent a copy of the paper.

riskLines.li: The one {FACTION}'s paper chose to print was of {A_nameDef} mid-sneeze, under a headline about frontier hardship. The silver was paid all the same.

lines.li: Blankets go up over the windows and the council keeps the usual hours. The light comes in round the edges anyway.
The council keeps everyone at work. At dusk a few walk out to the flowers anyway, and come back with the smell of them on their hands.
The colony keeps to its work, and the birds keep to theirs, building under every eave the colony has.
The colony puts buckets under the leaks and waits. The rain goes on drumming on the roof as if it has nowhere else to be.
The council keeps the colony near the walls while the stags are roaring. The bellowing goes on {PLACE} without anyone going to look.
{X_nameDef} hears the answer at the road, looks up at the colony for a while, and goes. {A_nameDef} doesn't come down to see {X_objective} off.
{X_nameDef} is brought in, and {A_nameDef} doesn't let go of {X_possessive} sleeve all afternoon, as if {X_nameDef} might vanish again.
{X_nameDef} stays. {A_nameDef} has been laughing more than usual, and some of the colony have started laying bets.
{X_nameDef} is told no, and goes without a scene. {A_nameDef} works late that night and says it was nothing.
The creditor counts the silver into a pouch and writes "paid" across the old note. {A_nameDef} reads the word twice.
The creditor is told no and goes, without threats. {A_nameDef} watches the road for a while afterward.
The bounty is carried out to the gate for the hunters to count, and they go. {A_nameDef}'s old life is paid off at last.
{X_nameDef} is taken back to {ENEMY} under the colony's guard, and doesn't say a word the whole way. {ENEMY} are pleased with the colony, and say so.

{B_nameDef} carried {X_nameDef}'s coat to market, wet and torn, and told the story of the river so well that one of the listeners wept. {X_nameDef} is one of the colony now, and drowned as far as {ENEMY} know.
